article_title: Hybrid teaching after COVID-19: advantages, challenges and optimization strategies.
citation: Wang Xiaoran, Liu Jiangheng, Jia Shuwei, Hou Chunmei, Jiao Runsheng, Yan Yan, Ma Tengchuang, Zhang Ying, Liu Yanyan, Wen Haixia, Wang Yu-Feng, Zhu Hui, Liu Xiao-Yu. (2024). Hybrid teaching after COVID-19: advantages, challenges and optimization strategies. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05745-z
title: HBOPPPS hybrid teaching model with online resource library for Physiology at Harbin Medical University
description: HBOPPPS is a hybrid teaching method introduced in 2019 that incorporates online instructional techniques into the offline BOPPPS framework (Bridge-in, Objective, Pre-assessment, Participatory learning, Post-assessment, Summary). The team built an online resource set including "course-associated micro-lecture videos (85 in total, 5 ∼ 10 min/video)", science stories, lectures by renowned doctors, virtual simulation experiments and chapter tests. Pre-class course guidance was delivered through the "Xuexi Tong" mobile application, with in-class interactive elements such as sign-in procedures, multi-choice questions and task allocation.
requirements: An established offline BOPPPS teaching model
An online learning resource library and a mobile application for course guidance and interaction
constraints: Implemented for Physiology teaching at Harbin Medical University among undergraduate medical students
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students in Pharmacy, Clinical Pharmacy, Basic Medicine and Clinical Medicine programs
target_learning_goals: Understanding healthy human body functions in Physiology, linking preclinical and clinical courses
examples: Students received pre-class course guidance via the Xuexi Tong app covering course objectives and key knowledge, and used in-class online sign-in, quiz and response functions

Hybrid teaching after COVID-19: advantages, challenges and optimization strategies. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05745-z

article_title: Assessment of the effectiveness of BOPPPS-based hybrid teaching model in physiology education.
citation: Liu Xiao-Yu, Lu Chunmei, Zhu Hui, Wang Xiaoran, Jia Shuwei, Zhang Ying, Wen Haixia, Wang Yu-Feng. (2022). Assessment of the effectiveness of BOPPPS-based hybrid teaching model in physiology education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03269-y
title: HBOPPPS: a hybrid BOPPPS teaching model delivered through the Xuexi Tong mobile app in three stages
description: HBOPPPS is a hybrid teaching method that incorporates online teaching into the six BOPPPS components, delivered through the "Xuexi Tong" mobile app. It operates in three stages: before the lecture (posted guidance, 80 micro-lecture videos of 5–10 min, opening questions, science stories and clinical cases), during the lecture (app sign-in, bridge-in stimuli, app-administered pre-assessment with automatic answer statistics, participatory learning with group discussion and student presentations, post-assessment with 3–5 multi-choice questions, and summary), and after the lecture (a teacher-posted mind map, student-posted course summaries, and online question-and-answer discussion). The app also generates an online score of students' learning initiatives.
requirements: Students are required to watch the micro-lecture videos completely before the lecture, and the model depends on the mobile app for sign-in, quiz administration, automatic answer statistics, and online discussion
constraints: The article notes minor differences in HBOPPPS components among different teachers, such as options for interpreting the micro-video lecture or using pre-assessment with the quiz following the bridge-in
target_learning_goals: systematic learning of Physiology course content
examples: Before introducing respiratory functions, teachers mentioned respiratory symptoms of COVID-19 patients or broadcast a heavy breathing sound to attract students' attention; a smartphone shake randomly selected students to answer questions
key_sources: Liu Xiao-Yu, Lu Chunmei, Zhu Hui, Wang Xiaoran, Jia Shuwei, Zhang Ying, Wen Haixia, Wang Yu-Feng. (2022). Assessment of the effectiveness of BOPPPS-based hybrid teaching model in physiology education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03269-y

article_title: Helping Babies Breathe, Second Edition: A Model for Strengthening Educational Programs to Increase Global Newborn Survival.
citation: Kamath-Rayne BD, Thukral A, Visick MK, Schoen E, Amick E, Deorari A, Cain CJ, Keenan WJ, Singhal N, Little GA, Niermeyer S. (2018). Helping Babies Breathe, Second Edition: A Model for Strengthening Educational Programs to Increase Global Newborn Survival. Global Health: Science and Practice. https://doi.org/10.9745/GHSP-D-18-00147
title: Helping Babies Breathe second edition curriculum and facilitator flip chart with expanded facilitator role
description: The second edition of HBB is a skills-based neonatal resuscitation curriculum for birth attendants in resource-limited settings, updated with 2015 ILCOR CoSTR science, a revised action plan, and a facilitator flip chart in which each page carries background information and educational advice for active learning techniques. The flip chart guides facilitators before, during, and after a course, encourages integrating workshops within local health care programs, and supports an expanded role in which facilitators enable learning and facilitate linkages with clinic leadership for ongoing practice and quality improvement.
requirements: Facilitators must provide supportive supervision after the workshop concludes and oversee establishment of a system for practice
constraints: Materials are freely downloadable at hbs.aap.org, with advice available for adapting first edition materials where printing new batches is difficult
target_learners: Birth attendants, nurses, midwives, and physicians in low-resource settings
target_learning_goals: Basic neonatal resuscitation within the Golden Minute after birth
examples: Two pages channel post-workshop enthusiasm into facility-level change via three questions: what will you do differently, what will you no longer do, and how will you make these changes happen
key_sources: Kamath-Rayne BD, Thukral A, Visick MK, Schoen E, Amick E, Deorari A, Cain CJ, Keenan WJ, Singhal N, Little GA, Niermeyer S. (2018). Helping Babies Breathe, Second Edition: A Model for Strengthening Educational Programs to Increase Global Newborn Survival. Global Health: Science and Practice. https://doi.org/10.9745/GHSP-D-18-00147

article_title: Helping Babies Breathe (HBB) training: What happens to knowledge and skills over time?
citation: Bang Akash; Patel Archana; Bellad Roopa; Gisore Peter; Goudar Shivaprasad S.; Esamai Fabian; Liechty Edward A.; Meleth Sreelatha; Goco Norman; Niermeyer Susan; Keenan William; Kamath-Rayne Beena D.; Little George A.; Clarke Susan B.; Flanagan Victoria A.; Bucher Sherri; Jain Manish; Mujawar Nilofer; Jain Vinita; Rukunga Janet; Mahantshetti Niranjana; Dhaded Sangappa; Bhandankar Manisha; McClure Elizabeth M.; Carlo Waldemar A.; Wright Linda L.; Hibberd Patricia L. (2016). Helping Babies Breathe (HBB) training: What happens to knowledge and skills over time?. BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12884-016-1141-3
title: Two-level master-trainer cascade with small-group hands-on simulation training
description: The article's training design pairs experienced central and country master trainers to train facility-level master trainers in a four-day hands-on course, who then deliver three-day facility courses to birth attendants. It used "A maximum ratio of 6 trainees:1 trainer", "Maximal opportunities to practice in trainee groups of 6", and "Before and after formal testing of knowledge and skills". The goal was to train at least one master trainer per facility to minimize the training cascade and roll out training in all facilities simultaneously, with roving monitors observing and providing feedback.
requirements: At least one trained facility-level master trainer per facility
Neonatal simulators and teaching materials (Learner Workbook, Facilitator Flip Chart, Action Plan poster) for each training group of six
constraints: Refresher training was restricted to active birth attendants who regularly attended deliveries, based on delivery logs
target_learners: Facility birth attendants in resource-limited settings
examples: Country-level four-day training of facility master trainers in May 2012, followed by three-day facility-level birth-attendant training between June and October 2012
